questions.answer: Traveling costs are low, but when you travel a lot it adds up.

questions.answer: Alcohol and groceries  are expensive, while takeaway is cheap.

Additional comments:
What kinds of cultural, athletic and social activities were available for students at your host institution? *
questions.answer: All sports I could think of were available. Lost of social activities if you live in a hall.

questions.question: Which non -academic activities would you recommend to future exchange students? Why? *
questions.answer: Do a sports activity, although be prepared to spend a lot of time on it.

questions.question: What do you recommend other visiting students see or do on their weekends or holidays? *
questions.answer: Make sure you have Fridays or Mondays off so you can go to Malaysia, Vietnam, etc.

questions.question: How easy was it to adjust to the local culture of your exchange site? *
questions.answer: Fairly easy as they speak English

questions.question: Do you have any tips for socializing with local students?
questions.answer: It’s hard, as Singaporeans are very private if you don’t have anything in common. All exchange students are very open though.

questions.question: What, if any, cultural differences did you find particularly challenging? *
questions.answer: Singaporeans are younger when they start university.

questions.question: What parts of the culture did you most appreciate? *
questions.answer: That is was very different depending on where in Singapore you went.

questions.question: What are the three most important things you would tell a UCPH student who is going to your host institution on exchange? *
questions.answer:
Participate in as much as possible. It will cool down after the first 3 weeks.

Go for the on campus housing and choose PGP or Utown for the best chances.

questions.question: Is there any other information that you think might prove useful to future exchange students attending your host institution? *
questions.answer: Have fun, don’t get too stressed about the exams. If you prepare accordingly you will go just fine.

questions.question: What was the most rewarding part of your exchange experience? *
questions.answer: Traveling

questions.question: What was the greatest challenge during the exchange? *
questions.answer: The first days when you were on your own and had to create a lot of new friendships.

questions.question: Any other comments?
Do you agree to share your travel report with other fellow students? *
questions.answer: Yes
